relationships.description: The operation's outcome map collects, through its individual Response entries, the response header declarations (such as X-RateLimit-Remaining or Location) that the operation can return across its status codes, and those headers may also live independently in the components headers registry.
relationships.evidence: Under an operation's responses block, one or more status-code entries declare a headers map whose entries are inline Header objects or $ref pointers to components/headers.

relationships.description: The operation's outcome map gathers the body schemas that describe the payload shape returned for each status code, while named schemas remain reusable definitions that exist independently under components/schemas.
relationships.evidence: Within an operation's responses block, status-code entries contain content media types whose schema property holds an inline schema or a $ref to components/schemas.

relationships.description: The operation's set of possible outcomes is related to the throttling policy governing that operation, typically because it includes a 429 Too Many Requests entry and rate-limit headers that report or signal the policy's enforcement.
relationships.evidence: The operation carrying the rate-limit extension or policy declares a '429' key in its responses map, or its responses define X-RateLimit-* or Retry-After headers matching the policy's window and limit.

relationships.description: Each Response object is one status-code-keyed outcome that exists only as an entry in an operation's outcome map, so removing the map or the operation removes that outcome.
relationships.evidence: The OpenAPI document lists the Response object, or a $ref to components/responses, under a status-code or 'default' key inside a specific operation's responses block.

relationships.description: The operation's outcome map points to the follow-on Link descriptors declared on its Response entries, telling clients which operation can be called next using values taken from this operation's results.
relationships.evidence: A status-code entry in the operation's responses block declares a links map whose entries name an operationId or operationRef, or $ref a definition under components/links.

relationships.description: The operation's outcome map points by $ref to named, shared schemas in components/schemas that define the body shapes of its outcomes, without owning those definitions.
relationships.evidence: A content media type under one of the operation's status-code entries holds a schema property of the form $ref: '#/components/schemas/...'.

notes: Headers, schemas and links properly belong to individual Response objects (or MediaType), not the Responses map; these are transitive shortcuts. aggregates.api.schema and references.api.schema largely overlap—distinguish inline versus $ref or drop one. RateLimit association is indirect and better attached to the operation or a 429 Response.
